story.title: A river under one wing
story.letter: The bird has tucked a river under its wing. Send this small beginning; there is room for the rest to follow.
story.goal: Make and send Riverwing.
story.sentCaption: A small beginning, carried by a wing.

story.title: A cup with other plans
story.letter: A fern has moved into the teacup. It seems to have mistaken the handle for a garden gate.
story.goal: Make and send Fern Cup.
story.sentCaption: Tea was expected. A garden arrived.

story.title: The bird finds a key
story.letter: A key has slipped between the feathers. Perhaps the bird is a map. Perhaps the map is learning to fly.
story.goal: Make and send Wayfinder.
story.sentCaption: A feather, a key, a way through.

story.title: Two ways to carry water
story.letter: A river under a wing; a moon above a cup. Put these two small journeys in the same envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Riverwing and Nightgarden.
story.sentCaption: The river and the cup met by post.

story.title: The opening is the picture
story.letter: The bird has opened in the middle. Leave that little gap for whatever might arrive next.
story.goal: Make and send Aviary Gate.
story.sentCaption: A gate made from the space between wings.

story.title: A short note after dark
story.letter: The fern has leaned sideways to make room for the moon. A small night garden can travel in a very short letter.
story.goal: Make and send Nightgarden.
story.sentCaption: One cup was enough room for the night.

story.title: A way through the arbor
story.letter: The bird brings its key to the fern's open arch. Neither picture quite explains the other. They seem pleased to meet.
story.goal: Make and send Wayfinder and Moonlit Arbor.
story.sentCaption: A key visited a garden with no door.

story.title: Two openings, one address
story.letter: The wing leaves a gap. The fern makes an arch. Send the two openings together and let the paper between them be a path.
story.goal: Make and send Aviary Gate and Moonlit Arbor.
story.sentCaption: The space between two pictures became a path.

story.title: A garden, by air
story.letter: The feathers have become a field. A small leaf has found the key. Let the whole unlikely garden travel by air.
story.goal: Make and send Wandering Aviary.
story.sentCaption: A garden folded itself into a wing.

story.title: The key writes back
story.letter: Here is the key again, carrying a frond this time. Send it beside the river-winged bird, as if they have something to tell each other.
story.goal: Make and send Frond Key and Riverwing.
story.sentCaption: The key returned with a leaf.

story.title: A crossing after dark
story.letter: The key lifts a bridge toward the night garden. OVER is written on it. What is on the other side can wait.
story.goal: Make and send Drawbridge Key and Nightgarden.
story.sentCaption: A bridge crossed the edge of a cup.

story.title: A crescent, by bird
story.letter: The moon needed a lift. The bird offered its back. This seems as good a postal arrangement as any.
story.goal: Make and send Crescent Courier.
story.sentCaption: The bird agreed to carry the moon.

story.title: Up, by another route
story.letter: The key has become a staircase. Its little UP scrap points the other way. Send the question along with the steps.
story.goal: Make and send Stairway Key.
story.sentCaption: The staircase kept the question open.

story.title: A bridge meets a boat
story.letter: The moon has folded itself into a skiff. The key offers a bridge. Two ways across, with no agreement about the water.
story.goal: Make and send Lunar Skiff and Drawbridge Key.
story.sentCaption: The same crossing, answered twice.

story.title: A place to come down
story.letter: The balloon says DOWN; the garden leaves a space beneath its moon. Send them together. Perhaps one has found a place in the other.
story.goal: Make and send Crescent Balloon and Moonlit Arbor.
story.sentCaption: The sky found a gap in the garden.

story.title: Here, with room for elsewhere
story.letter: The key has made a route from HERE to ELSE. The balloon has brought its own direction. Leave room in the envelope for both.
story.goal: Make and send Elsewhere Key and Crescent Balloon.
story.sentCaption: Here and elsewhere fitted in one envelope.

story.title: The higher low point
story.letter: The river has folded a hill into the map. LOW sits at the higher summit. Let the small disagreement travel.
story.goal: Make and send River Ridge.
story.sentCaption: The map sent a hill and kept its question.

story.title: A crossing with a passenger
story.letter: The map leaves a gap where the river crosses. The moon has brought its skiff. Send two answers to the same water.
story.goal: Make and send River Crossing and Lunar Skiff.
story.sentCaption: A gap in the map met a boat from the sky.

story.title: A small sip by air
story.letter: The cup lets one ribbon rise. The bird carries one strip of river. Both have found a small way out.
story.goal: Make and send Ribbon Sip and Riverwing.
story.sentCaption: A sip and a river travelled lightly.

story.title: Still water, quiet steam
story.letter: The river says STILL while falling down the paper. The divided cup says HUSH. Send the two conversations together.
story.goal: Make and send River Cascade and Tea Chorus.
story.sentCaption: The water moved. The steam kept its own counsel.

story.title: The cup visits its garden
story.letter: The cup has split into two voices. The old garden remembers its handle. Let the familiar shape arrive by another route.
story.goal: Make and send Tea Chorus and Moonlit Arbor.
story.sentCaption: The cup found its handle in an older letter.

story.title: Two ways to fold a river
story.letter: One picture opens upward. The other steps down. Send the fan of steam beside the river, with room between their directions.
story.goal: Make and send Pleated Steam and River Cascade.
story.sentCaption: The folds disagreed about which way was up.

story.title: Inland, with a way out
story.letter: The map has gathered three small towers. INLAND and OUT share the river. There is room for both addresses on this picture.
story.goal: Make and send River Citadel.
story.sentCaption: The river reached a place with more than one address.

story.title: A fold answers a fold
story.letter: The lantern has opened like a small accordion. The map has kept its two peaks. Send one fold to visit another.
story.goal: Make and send Folded Glow and River Ridge.
story.sentCaption: Two folded papers found different ways to stand.

story.title: A visitor at the window
story.letter: The roof has slipped sideways. INSIDE sits outside. The bird arrives carrying its crescent, without asking which side is home.
story.goal: Make and send Lantern House and Crescent Courier.
story.sentCaption: A moon-bearing bird found a window.

story.title: Two houses, one envelope
story.letter: Keep the two houses side by side for this letter. Their roofs need not become a tower to have something to say.
story.goal: Make and send 2 copies of Lantern House.
story.sentCaption: Two houses travelled without becoming one.

story.title: A tower with a loose end
story.letter: The windows have become a tower. The ribbon loops back toward its spool. ABOVE and AGAIN can share the same envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Lantern Tower and Ribbon Spool.
story.sentCaption: One shape rose; the other came round again.

story.title: A short note through the door
story.letter: A sip of steam and a leafy key make a small reply. The larger pictures can stay on the table a little longer.
story.goal: Make and send Ribbon Sip and Frond Key.
story.sentCaption: The cup and the key made a brief visit.

story.title: Three loops and a fold
story.letter: The ribbon has opened into three loops. The lantern spreads its paper windows. Send these two ways of opening together.
story.goal: Make and send Ribbon Bloom and Folded Glow.
story.sentCaption: A loop became a bloom beside a fold.

story.title: A window beside a weave
story.letter: The tower has windows. The loom has crossings. Let the light and the ribbon take turns filling the spaces between them.
story.goal: Make and send Lantern Tower and Ribbon Loom.
story.sentCaption: The window and the weave left room for the paper.

story.title: A route in the feathers
story.letter: The new wing has turned its feather lines into roads. The old river map has supplied two peaks. Put them together; an address might be a place between pictures.
story.goal: Make and send River Wing and River Ridge.
story.sentCaption: The river recognized a road in the wing.

story.title: A window receives a flower
story.letter: The bird is looking through its address window. Send the ribbon bloom to that little opening. A flower can be a perfectly good way of saying where you are.
story.goal: Make and send Address Window and Ribbon Bloom.
story.sentCaption: A ribbon flower reached the window.

story.title: Tea along the route
story.letter: The shoe has a route between heel and toe. The cups are sending steam in opposite directions. They can disagree about the journey and still share an envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Route and Tea Chorus.
story.sentCaption: The route travelled in good company.

story.title: Between here and there
story.letter: Two map-wings stand apart, with a red line between them. The shoe brings a whole walking route. Which sort of distance fits on this piece of paper?
story.goal: Make and send Here and There and Route.
story.sentCaption: The wings and the sole compared routes.

story.title: A small place to stay
story.letter: The long shoe-strip has met an upright little doorway. The bird is still at its window. Send these two addresses together, with the space between them left open.
story.goal: Make and send Address Window and Stay.
story.sentCaption: A doorway answered a window.

story.title: Go, with a roof
story.letter: GO sits beneath an arch of shoe fragments. The lantern house offers a large roof and a window. They make a fine travelling address, even if the roof stays behind.
story.goal: Make and send Go and Lantern House.
story.sentCaption: The shoe found a roof to write to.

story.title: The shape of arrival
story.letter: The bird has reached a window shaped like a bird. The route between them is all angles. Send this arrival whenever it is ready; other addresses can still have their turn.
story.goal: Make and send Arrival.
story.sentCaption: A bird-shaped space received the bird.

story.title: A chair with a view
story.letter: The chair back has spread into three little windows. Send the view when you like. There will be time to decide who sits beside it.
story.goal: Make and send Window.
story.sentCaption: Three openings made a quiet beginning.

story.title: The fern takes a seat
story.letter: SIT is printed under the chair’s open seat. The fern has brought its own cup. Leave the two pictures together, as if a visit could be that simple.
story.goal: Make and send Invitation and Fern Cup.
story.sentCaption: The fern arrived with its cup.

story.title: A handle full of steam
story.letter: The new cup has given most of its room to the handle. The old cup has made a fan of steam. One has an opening; the other has something light to put beside it.
story.goal: Make and send Full and Pleated Steam.
story.sentCaption: The steam found room beside the handle.

story.title: No need to fill it
story.letter: The chair leaves its seat open. The two cup fragments meet at a narrow red waist. Send the empty places together, without finding anything to fill them.
story.goal: Make and send Invitation and Empty.
story.sentCaption: The empty places kept one another company.

story.title: An answer with windows
story.letter: The cup’s answer has a round gap in its middle. The chair replies with three windows. This conversation seems to need very little ink.
story.goal: Make and send Answer and Window.
story.sentCaption: The round answer met the open view.

story.title: Flowers while we wait
story.letter: The chair fragments face each other across a red strip. Bring the ribbon bloom from the studio. Waiting is part of this picture, never a task for you.
story.goal: Make and send Wait and Ribbon Bloom.
story.sentCaption: A ribbon bloom sat beside the gap.

story.title: A pair of pairs
story.letter: PAIR sits at the hinge of each picture. This letter needs two separate Pair Hinges. Keep them side by side for the envelope instead of merging them into Seed Leaf.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Pair Hinge pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two Pair Hinges travelled as a pair.

story.title: A seed and a handle
story.letter: The pear has become a frame around its seed. The cup has made its handle much larger. Send these two ways of keeping a small thing in sight.
story.goal: Make and send Seed Leaf and Full.
story.sentCaption: The seed and the cup each kept their opening.

story.title: A tide for the skiff
story.letter: The fish has a blue wave between head and tail. The moon’s little skiff has a sail. Put their waters in the same envelope and let the paper do the floating.
story.goal: Make and send Tide and Lunar Skiff.
story.sentCaption: The skiff met a tide made of fish.

story.title: Two seeds, separately
story.letter: Two Seed Leaves belong in this reply. The next picture would be Split, but these two are staying separate for the journey. Count the pictures, even if their names start a game.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Seed Leaf pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two seeds kept their own frames.

story.title: A bridge above the tide
story.letter: The pear curve and leaf stand apart on a red bridge. The fish sends a blue wave below its head. These pieces have found a crossing without becoming a map.
story.goal: Make and send Split and Tide.
story.sentCaption: The pear’s bridge met the fish’s tide.

story.title: See where to go
story.letter: SEE has an eye above it. GO has an arch above it. Send the two pictures together. The words can offer advice; the exact pieces are all the letter needs.
story.goal: Make and send Lookout and Go.
story.sentCaption: SEE and GO went by the same post.

story.title: Facing a pair
story.letter: The fish head looks across a wide gap toward its tail. The pear halves open from their hinge. Send these two conversations between parts of the same picture.
story.goal: Make and send Facing and Pair Hinge.
story.sentCaption: The fish and pear recognized their other halves.

story.title: Loops in company
story.letter: The scissors have spread their handles into unequal loops. The ribbon rises in a loop of its own. Send them together; neither needs to hold anything shut.
story.goal: Make and send Loops and Ribbon Spool.
story.sentCaption: Three loops shared a small envelope.

story.title: A join and a crossing
story.letter: A red bar joins the two scissor strips. The key lifts its shaft into a bridge. Both leave a gap beneath the part that reaches across.
story.goal: Make and send Join and Drawbridge Key.
story.sentCaption: The join and the bridge left their gaps open.

story.title: One stitch on the route
story.letter: The button’s two halves are held at the left by a red stitch. The shoe has a red route of its own. They can travel together without being sewn to each other.
story.goal: Make and send Clasp and Route.
story.sentCaption: A stitch kept pace with the walking route.

story.title: Over the windows
story.letter: A long scissor blade runs above two handles. The button has opened four windows in a row. Lay their two kinds of line beside each other for this reply.
story.goal: Make and send Overcut and Threadway.
story.sentCaption: The blade and the windows made two lines.

story.title: Eight windows, two pictures
story.letter: This envelope needs two Threadways, each with its own four windows. Keep the two pieces separate. A larger button picture would answer a different letter.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Threadway pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two Threadways kept all eight windows.

story.title: An opening and its company
story.letter: The button stitches surround a tilted diamond. The scissor handles have made two rounder openings. Send them together as a small collection of useful spaces.
story.goal: Make and send Open and Loops.
story.sentCaption: A diamond travelled beside two loops.

story.title: A quiet join
story.letter: The scissors hold their gap with a red bar. The cups have a HUSH scrap between their steam curls. A join can be a quiet thing.
story.goal: Make and send Join and Tea Chorus.
story.sentCaption: The cups kept the join quiet.

story.title: A wave and a clasp
story.letter: The hand is waving. The button is holding two halves together with one stitch. Send a greeting that can travel without anyone having to let go.
story.goal: Make and send Wave and Clasp.
story.sentCaption: The wave reached the little clasp.

story.title: A greeting with a seat
story.letter: Two thumbs have met between their cuffs. The chair has left a seat open. Send the introduction and the invitation together.
story.goal: Make and send Meet and Invitation.
story.sentCaption: The greeting found a place to sit.

story.title: An introduction over a cup
story.letter: Two profiles face a slim line of light. The cup has brought its large handle. A little space and something to drink from: that is enough for an introduction.
story.goal: Make and send Introduction and Full.
story.sentCaption: The profiles met beside the cup.

story.title: Inside the greeting
story.letter: The hands meet at their thumbs. The face opens around an eye-shaped gap. There is someone in this conversation, even where the paper is missing.
story.goal: Make and send Meet and Inside.
story.sentCaption: The open face received the joined hands.

story.title: An aside, with a wave
story.letter: The nose and jaw have made an open corner. Add the waving hand, as if one small remark had caught your attention on the way past.
story.goal: Make and send Aside and Wave.
story.sentCaption: The aside caught a wave.

story.title: A direction worth seeing
story.letter: The pointing finger and palm leave a corner between them. The fish has put SEE under its eye. Perhaps the hand is showing the eye where to look.
story.goal: Make and send Between and Lookout.
story.sentCaption: The hand offered the eye a direction.

story.title: The wing calls back
story.letter: The receiver has stood up on its cord. The map-wing is here again, with roads among its feathers. Let the old route answer this new shape.
story.goal: Make and send Off Hook and River Wing.
story.sentCaption: The wing answered the upright receiver.

story.title: A crossed connection
story.letter: A black-and-ivory receiver crosses the dial beside a red BUSY scrap. The river drops through a broken crossing. Send their crossed lines together, without asking either to straighten out.
story.goal: Make and send Busy and River Crossing.
story.sentCaption: The dial and the river crossed paths.

story.title: A hat for GO
story.letter: The bowler tips its crown. The shoe has left GO beneath its arch. One is a greeting; the other may already be on its way.
story.goal: Make and send Tip and Go.
story.sentCaption: The tipped hat caught the passing shoe.

story.title: Listening to a salute
story.letter: The receiver ends face a diamond of air. The hat brim spreads like a broad greeting. The hat has plenty to say without making a sound.
story.goal: Make and send Listening and Salute.
story.sentCaption: The receivers listened to the spread brim.

story.title: A familiar face
story.letter: The greeting made from a hat returns to the open face. Send them together. An introduction can become familiar without needing a longer speech.
story.goal: Make and send Salute and Inside.
story.sentCaption: The hat greeted the face again.

story.title: Hello from above
story.letter: The crown strip sits high above its brim. The receiver has stretched upward too. Send these two pictures reaching out of their ordinary shapes.
story.goal: Make and send Overhead and Off Hook.
story.sentCaption: The receiver and crown reached up together.

story.title: Until another time
story.letter: The telephone cord curls into a question. The hat gives one more small tip. Send them when you are ready; the question belongs to the drawing.
story.goal: Make and send Call Again and Tip.
story.sentCaption: A tipped hat answered the curled question.

story.title: A small part
story.letter: The comb has opened into two banks of teeth. The red hinge keeps them near each other. A short reply is quite enough for this picture.
story.goal: Make and send Part.
story.sentCaption: The teeth left a little part between them.

story.title: Three loops, uneven teeth
story.letter: The comb’s teeth take turns down a stepped spine. The ribbon bloom has three broad loops. Put their different rhythms on one sheet.
story.goal: Make and send Rhythm and Ribbon Bloom.
story.sentCaption: The loops and teeth kept different rhythms.

story.title: A tick held by a stitch
story.letter: The watch has become two upright arcs. The button holds its halves with one stitch. Neither picture needs you to count seconds.
story.goal: Make and send Tick and Clasp.
story.sentCaption: A small stitch travelled beside a tick.

story.title: Room for a pause
story.letter: The comb makes a low arch above its red line. One tooth sits apart. Send the space they leave; you need not wait to make a pause.
story.goal: Make and send Pause.
story.sentCaption: The pause was already in the paper.

story.title: Between the parts
story.letter: A minute hand reaches between the watch’s distant halves. The comb leaves a narrower part between its teeth. Send these two measures of empty space.
story.goal: Make and send Interval and Part.
story.sentCaption: The long interval met the narrow part.

story.title: After the greeting
story.letter: The broken watch face steps downward. The hat still holds its greeting wide. Put them together without deciding how much time has passed.
story.goal: Make and send After and Salute.
story.sentCaption: The greeting travelled beside the broken clock.

story.title: A rhythm with room
story.letter: The comb’s steps and the watch’s far-apart halves fit in one reply. Some marks gather; others leave room. The rhythm is in how you look at them.
story.goal: Make and send Rhythm and Interval.
story.sentCaption: The teeth and dial left room for each other.

story.title: The river returns
story.letter: The envelope has opened into a diamond. The first bird still carries its river under a wing. Send them together; an opening makes a fine return address.
story.goal: Make and send Open Letter and Riverwing.
story.sentCaption: The river-winged bird found an open letter.

story.title: Forward, around the dial
story.letter: The folded letter points onward. The telephone dial has finger holes around its ivory center. This reply can have both a direction and a place to turn around.
story.goal: Make and send Forward and Busy.
story.sentCaption: The arrow passed the ring of finger holes.

story.title: An ear beside an eye
story.letter: The shell has curled around a listening space. The fish brings its eye above SEE. Send these two small ways of paying attention.
story.goal: Make and send Ear and Lookout.
story.sentCaption: The shell listened beside the fish’s eye.

story.title: Sound goes forward
story.letter: The postal folds make a zigzag arrow. The shell halves hold a shallow wave-shaped opening. Send the direction beside the sound it might carry.
story.goal: Make and send Forward and Sound.
story.sentCaption: The shell’s wave went with the folded arrow.

story.title: A reply with steam
story.letter: Two letter flaps face a gap between them. The cup returns with its fan of steam. Perhaps the old tea conversation has found another page.
story.goal: Make and send Reply and Pleated Steam.
story.sentCaption: The steam rose beside a paper reply.

story.title: A whisper for the skiff
story.letter: The shell offers a quiet right-angle corner. The moon brings its small sailboat back. A long journey can receive a very short message.
story.goal: Make and send Whisper and Lunar Skiff.
story.sentCaption: The skiff received the shell’s quiet corner.

story.title: The loom gets a letter
story.letter: The open envelope and the ribbon loom both leave room inside. Send the two frames together, like a note to the studio where the ribbons began.
story.goal: Make and send Open Letter and Ribbon Loom.
story.sentCaption: An open letter visited the loom.

story.title: What the shell kept
story.letter: The shell ribs rise into a broad crest, with an open bite beneath the edge. Send the shape it has made from listening. The other replies can still find their own order.
story.goal: Make and send Resonance.
story.sentCaption: The shell sent the space it had kept.

story.title: A hat beside a folded sky
story.letter: The umbrella has folded around its hooked handle. The bowler gives a small tip. They look ready to pass each other in a very narrow doorway.
story.goal: Make and send Furled and Tip.
story.sentCaption: The folded umbrella passed the tipped hat.

story.title: A gust goes forward
story.letter: The umbrella has turned inside out. The letter still points forward through its zigzag folds. Send their two directions without asking the wind to agree.
story.goal: Make and send Gust and Forward.
story.sentCaption: The gust and the letter went onward together.

story.title: A crossing for an anchor
story.letter: The tilted anchor has one long fluke. The river map leaves a broken crossing. Put the two beside each other; this anchor can visit the river on paper.
story.goal: Make and send Afloat and River Crossing.
story.sentCaption: The anchor reached the river crossing.

story.title: A larger piece of weather
story.letter: The umbrella folds rise in three steps, with the broad hook curling below. This is a longer picture to make. It can keep its place while you choose another available letter.
story.goal: Make and send Fair Weather.
story.sentCaption: Three folds carried their own weather.

story.title: A crescent and a fold
story.letter: Two anchor flukes make a low crescent. The umbrella keeps its canopy folded tight. Send these two compact shapes between the larger weather reports.
story.goal: Make and send Moor and Furled.
story.sentCaption: The flukes and the folded canopy fitted together.

story.title: Drift with a sound
story.letter: The anchor stock turns a corner above its fluke. The shell holds a wave of empty space. Let the drifting picture have something quiet to travel beside.
story.goal: Make and send Drift and Sound.
story.sentCaption: The drift went beside the shell’s wave.

story.title: Upward, with a mooring
story.letter: The gust lifts the umbrella ribs. The anchor flukes hold their low curve. Send the lifted and the low picture in one envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Gust and Moor.
story.sentCaption: The gust had a low crescent for company.

story.title: Two bees, still separate
story.letter: This letter needs two separate Be Still pictures. Each bee keeps its folded wing. Merging them would make In Between, which belongs to another request.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Be Still pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two resting bees shared the envelope.

story.title: Between the leaves and moon
story.letter: The bee’s striped body crosses its uneven wings. The old fern cup holds a moon. Send a garden visit made from these two pictures.
story.goal: Make and send In Between and Nightgarden.
story.sentCaption: The bee visited the little night garden.

story.title: A double and a tick
story.letter: The domino faces meet at a right angle. The watch arcs rise on their stem. Their names sound short; their shapes have room for a conversation.
story.goal: Make and send Double and Tick.
story.sentCaption: The double met the upright tick.

story.title: Two ways of being between
story.letter: Keep two In Between pictures separate for this envelope. Their wings can face one another on the table. A single Be Side would be a different reply.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate In Between pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two striped crossings stayed separate.

story.title: Beside the double
story.letter: The bee steps upward beside its broad wing. The domino turns a low corner. Send the two shapes together and let each keep its own direction.
story.goal: Make and send Be Side and Double.
story.sentCaption: The bee stood beside the domino corner.

story.title: Two tumbles
story.letter: Each Tumble has its own diagonal of pips. This letter needs two of them, kept separate. The envelope can hold two falling lines without turning them into a bracket.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Tumble pieces.
story.sentCaption: Two lines of pips made the journey.

story.title: Pause here, little bee
story.letter: The domino leaves a bracket open at its side. The bee is resting beneath a folded wing. Send a place to pause beside a picture already quite good at it.
story.goal: Make and send Pause Here and Be Still.
story.sentCaption: The bee rested beside the open bracket.

story.title: A page receives a letter
story.letter: One page stands up from the book. The letter opens its middle. Slip the two pictures into the same envelope, like a note left at a useful page.
story.goal: Make and send Turn and Open Letter.
story.sentCaption: The open letter found the turning page.

story.title: A face in the folds
story.letter: The book has become a diagonal accordion. The profile leaves an eye-shaped space. Send the reader and the folded pages without filling in the missing face.
story.goal: Make and send Fold and Inside.
story.sentCaption: The folded pages met the open eye.

story.title: A little fan at the window
story.letter: Three printed matches spread from their cover. The lantern house brings its familiar window. These paper shapes can share their small light.
story.goal: Make and send Fan and Lantern House.
story.sentCaption: The matchbook fan visited the lantern window.

story.title: Two folds, one small fan
story.letter: Keep two folded books separate for this envelope. The matchbook spreads its three printed matches beside them. Send both Folds and the little Fan, with every page still its own.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Fold pieces and Fan.
story.sentCaption: Two folded books shared an envelope with the little fan.

story.title: A passage beside the handle
story.letter: The book’s pages fan away from their binding. The cup gives most of its room to a tall handle. Send the sweep of pages beside that generous opening.
story.goal: Make and send Passage and Full.
story.sentCaption: The fanned pages found room beside the handle.

story.title: After the small light
story.letter: The matchbook keeps its spent match. The book has another page ready to turn. Send them together; there is still one more chapter to read.
story.goal: Make and send Spent and Turn.
story.sentCaption: The spent match rested beside the turning page.

story.title: A bell opens the exchange
story.letter: The bell tips its mouth sideways. The comb has left a part between its teeth. Send a small opening to this last conversation.
story.goal: Make and send Tilt and Part.
story.sentCaption: The tilted bell met the parted comb.

story.title: A peal for the telephone
story.letter: Two bell halves spread around their handle. The telephone carries its red BUSY scrap. Send the two ways of calling, with no need for either to ring.
story.goal: Make and send Peal and Busy.
story.sentCaption: The bell and the telephone called on paper.

story.title: Paper for the folds
story.letter: A tall sheet rises from the typewriter. The book returns as its folded accordion. They have enough paper between them for a generous reply.
story.goal: Make and send Paper and Fold.
story.sentCaption: The fresh sheet met the folded pages.

story.title: Tell it on paper
story.letter: The bell lip has become a low bowl. The typewriter holds up its sheet. Put the telling picture beside somewhere for the words to go.
story.goal: Make and send Tell and Paper.
story.sentCaption: The bell’s bowl received a sheet of paper.

story.title: Return to the sound
story.letter: The typewriter carriage reaches across its keys. The shell sends its shallow wave again. A return can bring an old sound into a new line.
story.goal: Make and send Return and Sound.
story.sentCaption: The carriage returned beside the shell’s wave.

story.title: A small last light
story.letter: The tilted bell visits the matchbook with its spent match. A picture can keep the trace of something without asking you to make it happen again.
story.goal: Make and send Tilt and Spent.
story.sentCaption: The bell kept company with the spent match.

story.title: A return for the wayfinder
story.letter: The typewriter carriage reaches beyond its keys. The old bird still has its key and its river feather. Send the traveller beside the returning carriage.
story.goal: Make and send Return and Wayfinder.
story.sentCaption: The wayfinder travelled beside the returning carriage.

story.title: The last line is written
story.letter: The paper strips gather above the typewriter’s keys. Cynthia, send Written as the last line of the campaign. There is room around it for everything you chose to keep.
story.goal: Make and send Written.
story.sentCaption: The last line is sent. The table is yours.

story.title: A mark for an open letter
story.letter: The stamp has turned on its side. The old letter has opened its folds. There is room for a mark along that waiting edge.
story.goal: Make and send Sideways and Open Letter.
story.sentCaption: The sideways stamp reached the open letter.

story.title: A little off the line
story.letter: The printing block has slipped into two steps beneath its handle. A fresh sheet rises from the typewriter. Put the offset mark beside the straight paper.
story.goal: Make and send Offset and Paper.
story.sentCaption: The stepped block met the fresh sheet.

story.title: An inkling at the margin
story.letter: The pen points sideways too, with a small opening between its tines. Its bent barrel and the turned stamp make a pair of unusual margins.
story.goal: Make and send Inkling and Sideways.
story.sentCaption: The nib and the stamp kept their sideways company.

story.title: Two separate impressions
story.letter: Keep two Offset pictures separate for this reply. Each has its own red join and stepped printing block. One Countermark is a different picture, even though it holds the same amount of paper.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Offset pictures.
story.sentCaption: Two Offset pictures travelled as a pair.

story.title: A mark around a gap
story.letter: The stamp leaves a long open rectangle between its printing strips. Set the split pen nib beside that space. A mark can be interesting for what it leaves untouched.
story.goal: Make and send Countermark and Inkling.
story.sentCaption: The open rectangle received the split nib.

story.title: Under the returning carriage
story.letter: The pen bends into an underline. The typewriter carriage reaches beyond its keys. These two long edges can share a letter without agreeing on where the line should end.
story.goal: Make and send Underline and Return.
story.sentCaption: The underline went beside the returning carriage.

story.title: Writing through
story.letter: The pen has opened an oval in its nib. The stamp keeps its small offset step. Let the last reply in this envelope have a space at its center.
story.goal: Make and send Written Through and Offset.
story.sentCaption: The open nib kept a place for the offset mark.

story.title: A sideways introduction
story.letter: The spectacle lenses have folded into a tall pair. The pen is still pointing sideways. Put the two directions together, then make room for a camera.
story.goal: Make and send Side Glance and Inkling.
story.sentCaption: The folded lenses met the sideways nib.

story.title: A longer view
story.letter: The camera stretches its bellows toward the lens. The spectacles keep their two rings close together. One view reaches out; the other folds in.
story.goal: Make and send Exposure and Side Glance.
story.sentCaption: The long camera stood beside the folded glasses.

story.title: Two offsets
story.letter: One spectacle rim opens at its edge. The camera has shifted into two stepped blocks. These are two different ways to leave a picture slightly unsettled.
story.goal: Make and send Overlook and Shutter.
story.sentCaption: The open rim and the stepped camera shared a reply.

story.title: Through the lower edge
story.letter: The lenses hang open beneath a broad bar. The camera extends its bellows along the table. Keep the lifted line and the long line together.
story.goal: Make and send Through and Exposure.
story.sentCaption: The hanging rims received the extended camera.

story.title: A window in the camera
story.letter: The camera frame has opened a square window beside its round lens. The folded spectacles bring another pair of openings. Leave the spaces clear.
story.goal: Make and send Viewfinder and Side Glance.
story.sentCaption: The camera window kept company with the folded lenses.

story.title: A still life to keep
story.letter: The camera panels spread across one another, with the round lens resting at the left. Nothing needs to move for this last picture. Send Still Life when it is ready.
story.goal: Make and send Still Life.
story.sentCaption: The camera settled into its still life.

story.title: An open pin and a clasp
story.letter: The pin has opened into a wide V. The old button still holds its two halves with a stitch. They can travel together without either having to close.
story.goal: Make and send Unfasten and Clasp.
story.sentCaption: The open pin visited the button clasp.

story.title: Room between the teeth
story.letter: The zipper tapes part into a Y, with their large teeth facing inward. Add the open pin. Both pictures have left plenty of room for the reply.
story.goal: Make and send Parted and Unfasten.
story.sentCaption: The parted zipper received the open pin.

story.title: A crooked approach
story.letter: The pin takes an S-shaped turn between its coil and clasp. The zipper offers two straight sides. Put the crooked route beside the parted one.
story.goal: Make and send Crooked Point and Parted.
story.sentCaption: The crooked pin reached the parted zipper.

story.title: Two open pins and a zigzag
story.letter: Keep two Unfasten pictures for the two sides of this reply, with one Zigzag between them. The zipper picture may also fit another available letter. Choose where you want that bend to go first.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Unfasten pictures and Zigzag.
story.sentCaption: Two open pins travelled with one zipper bend.

story.title: Join at the bend
story.letter: The zipper changes direction at a green paper joint. The old scissors have made Join from their printed loops. Let the two joins answer each other.
story.goal: Make and send Zigzag and Join.
story.sentCaption: The zipper joint met the scissors join.

story.title: A loop takes the long way
story.letter: The pin has drawn its coil into a large open circle. The zipper keeps its stepped bend. You can finish this loop before the two open pins, or leave it for later.
story.goal: Make and send Loopback and Zigzag.
story.sentCaption: The large coil travelled beside the zipper bend.

story.title: Held by a thread
story.letter: The zipper tapes cross at their green join. Threadway returns with its button holes and connecting thread. These small fastenings are enough to close this envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Interleave and Threadway.
story.sentCaption: The crossed tapes met the threaded button.

story.title: A short rule for a page
story.letter: Two ruler strips stand around a tall gap. The book is turning its pages. Leave a little space between the marks and the page edge.
story.goal: Make and send Short Rule and Turn.
story.sentCaption: The short rule found a place beside the turning book.

story.title: An angle left open
story.letter: The ruler has made a right angle. The pin still opens wider than its clasp. Neither picture needs to make a closed frame.
story.goal: Make and send Right Angle and Unfasten.
story.sentCaption: The right angle received the open pin.

story.title: A small measure
story.letter: The thimble has settled into two low dotted panels. The ruler keeps its narrow upright gap. A short reply will do for these ordinary pieces.
story.goal: Make and send Tilted and Short Rule.
story.sentCaption: The low thimble sat beside the short rule.

story.title: Two corners
story.letter: Keep two Right Angle pictures separate. One Out of Line picture would use the same paper, but this request has a place for two corners.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Right Angle pictures.
story.sentCaption: Two right angles kept their own corners.

story.title: Outside the line
story.letter: The ruler strips almost make a triangle, leaving a break near the top. The thimble joins a tall dotted wall to an open oval. Their openings do not have to match.
story.goal: Make and send Measure and Out of Line.
story.sentCaption: The broken triangle met the open thimble rim.

story.title: Enough room for a small reply
story.letter: The thimble leaves a broad opening above its rim. Put the ruler corner beside it. There is enough room here to close these four envelopes and keep the table for whatever comes next.
story.goal: Make and send Open Top and Right Angle.
story.sentCaption: The open thimble and the ruler corner finished the four envelopes.

chapters.title: Garden Correspondence
chapters.nextPreview: Keep your board and upgrades. The Key source opens when you enter Moonlit Correspondence; its first two letters open Moon.

chapters.title: Moonlit Correspondence
chapters.nextPreview: The river finds a map; the cup sends steam. Keep your table and open the free Map source. The first two Riverside letters open Teacup.

chapters.title: Riverside Reverie
chapters.nextPreview: A lantern answers the folds in the map. Keep your stock and upgrades; the first two Lantern letters open Spool.

chapters.title: Lantern Studio
chapters.nextPreview: A bird has an address in its feathers. A shoe has a route in its sole. Neither has agreed where the letter should go.

chapters.title: Wrong Address
chapters.nextPreview: Pull up a chair. The cup has already made itself comfortable. There is no need to fill every space between them.

chapters.title: Quiet Company
chapters.nextPreview: A pear has received a note addressed to a pair. A fish is looking into SEE. The pictures can enjoy the mix-up; the packing list stays exact.

chapters.title: Namesakes
chapters.nextPreview: The scissors brought an offcut. The button brought four holes. Put the small absences to work, without asking them to become anything else.

chapters.title: Useful Gaps
chapters.nextPreview: A pointing hand has met a profile. One has a direction; the other has a nose. A short introduction may be enough.

chapters.title: Small Talk
chapters.nextPreview: The telephone is off its hook. The hat is halfway through a greeting. An old picture would be welcome in this conversation.

chapters.title: Hello Again
chapters.nextPreview: The comb counts its teeth. The watch points between its numbers. You can give either picture the next turn; neither is timing you.

chapters.title: Off Beat
chapters.nextPreview: An envelope has come back with its folds rearranged. A shell is listening beside it. There may be room in the reply for something from the first letters.

chapters.title: Return Mail
chapters.nextPreview: An umbrella has turned inside out. An anchor has tilted toward the sky. A small reply can sit beside a longer one while they settle the weather between them.

chapters.title: Fair Weather
chapters.nextPreview: A bee has paused beside a double. There are several ways to arrange the next reply, and a pair of pictures need not become a single larger one.

chapters.title: Double Meaning
chapters.nextPreview: The book opens its pages; the matchbook opens its cover. A few familiar pictures can slip between them, like notes left by an earlier reader.

chapters.title: Fine Print
chapters.nextPreview: A bell has brought its clapper. A typewriter has brought a fresh sheet. After all these folded replies, there is room for a clear last line.

chapters.title: Sound Advice
chapters.nextPreview: All sixteen chapters are sent. Explore your collection, reread a letter, or return to isolated practice whenever you like.

chapters.title: Small Impressions
chapters.nextPreview: The spectacles fold their rims. The camera extends its bellows. This envelope has room for a quick introduction and a longer still life.

chapters.title: Second Look
chapters.nextPreview: A pin and a zipper arrive together. Both free sources are open. Keep a pair of small bends, make a larger loop, or finish the other available reply first.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.nextPreview: The ruler has only a few broad marks. The thimble is small enough to sit beside them. These last replies leave the measures modest.

chapters.title: Short Measure
chapters.nextPreview: These four extra correspondences are complete. Explore your collection or practice a sent letter. Further content is not required to keep this ending.
